whyEngineering: I've always liked shapes and patterns, and figuring out how things actually work rather than just using them. Engineering feels like it sits right at that intersection — problem-solving, making things, and building things that help people. Civil engineering in particular has caught my attention because it's all of that at a scale you can actually walk through and live in.
aspirationStatement: Dare to Dream: STEM Careers for Girls at UTS was one of the first times this felt real rather than just an idea — hearing from people who actually work in STEM and engineering made me start thinking, this might actually be what I want to do. I'm only in Year 9, though, so civil engineering is a strong current curiosity, not a decided plan. I'm planning to keep exploring — more STEM experiences, competitions, and eventually work experience — before I narrow anything down.
womenInEngineeringNote: Dare to Dream was specifically about STEM careers for girls, and it mattered to be in a room full of other girls asking the same questions I was, hearing from women who'd actually built careers in these fields. It made the idea feel a lot less abstract.
